title: Close a priced equity round
summary: Close a priced round (seed or Series A): term sheet, diligence, definitive documents, board and stockholder approvals, signatures, wires, and the cap table made true.

parts.title: Negotiate the term sheet
parts.guidance: Model the proposed term sheet’s effects on valuation, option-pool dilution, liquidation preferences, governance and participation rights against the current capitalization. Compare those outcomes with the fundraising goals and existing investor rights. Identify binding provisions with counsel and develop the founder’s negotiation positions, including terms that need board input.

parts.title: Sign the term sheet
parts.guidance: Check the final term sheet against the negotiated terms and understand its binding provisions, conditions and exclusivity commitments with counsel. The company signatory needs authority for the commitments being made. Once signed, use the executed terms to drive diligence and definitive documents, identifying any obligations or dates that now constrain the company.

parts.title: Refresh the data room for diligence
parts.guidance: Update the data room against the investor’s diligence request and proposed round. Reconcile capitalization, financials, contracts, IP records and corporate approvals to current versions, replacing superseded material and identifying gaps. Limit each investor’s access to the agreed scope and clear sensitive disclosures with their owner. Keep an index that lets reviewers locate the evidence behind each response.

parts.title: Investor diligence and Q&A
parts.guidance: Track investor questions against the requested evidence and the team member who can answer them. Verify substantive financial, legal and customer claims with that person, and route sensitive or privileged requests through the appropriate executive or counsel. Share the response through the agreed diligence channel and record whether it resolved the question or left a closing condition outstanding.

parts.title: Counsel drafts the definitive documents
parts.guidance: Give counsel the signed term sheet, existing corporate and equity documents, diligence findings and investor allocations. Review the definitive documents together for consistent economics, governance, disclosures and closing conditions. Compare revisions with the negotiated deal and resolve founder decisions as they arise. The resulting package should identify any approvals or conditions still needed before it can be executed and closed.

parts.title: Prepare and circulate the board and stockholder consents
parts.guidance: Draft the resolutions needed for the transaction with counsel or the corporate secretary. Reconcile share classes, issuance amounts, charter changes and reserved rights to the pro forma capitalization, then identify the directors or holders who must decide each action. Circulate the proposed resolutions with enough supporting material for those decisions, tracking revisions until the signature version is settled.

parts.title: Board and stockholders sign the consents
parts.guidance: Route the final consents to the directors and stockholders whose approval is required for this transaction. Check voting thresholds, signatory authority and conditions with counsel. Collect the signed resolutions and establish when the necessary approvals become effective, resolving changes before the closing team relies on them to issue securities.

parts.title: Route the closing packet for e-signature
parts.guidance: Match each closing document’s signature block to the correct person, entity and signing capacity. Check the final versions, side letters and any sequencing or release conditions set by counsel, then send the packet through the transaction’s authorized signing process. Track execution separately from permission to release documents and close; an assembled set of signatures may still have conditions outstanding.

parts.title: Verify the wires and issue the shares
parts.guidance: Reconcile incoming wires to investor allocations and resolve missing, partial or unexpected receipts. Counsel and the closing lead establish whether the documents, corporate authorizations and other conditions permit issuance. The authorized equity administrator records the specific shares released at closing, linking each allocation to funds and executed documents. Leave investors still awaiting completion separate from the completed close.

parts.title: File Form D with the SEC
parts.guidance: Determine the applicable post-closing filings from the issuer’s jurisdiction and actual transaction. Use the final issuance schedule, approvals and investor information to identify the required notices and deadlines with counsel. The company’s authorized filer submits the completed forms through the relevant official route and resolves rejected or incomplete submissions. Completion is the required filing outcome, with its receipt linked to the transaction.

options.title: Default — SEC EDGAR online forms
options.summary: For an offering requiring Form D, reconcile the notice to the executed transaction and first-sale date. Check the company’s EDGAR access and the filing individual’s assigned role. The authorized filer submits the reviewed notice and verifies its status, preserving the filed version and receipt. Identify amendments and state notices separately with counsel so the remaining offering obligations are visible.

references.title: SEC Filing a Form D Notice

verify.how: The accepted Form D appears under the company's name in EDGAR full-text search within about a business day.

cost.note: The SEC charges no filing fee for a Form D notice or amendment; most states charge their own blue-sky notice-filing fees.

options.title: India - PAS-3 private placement
options.summary: For an Indian allotment, establish the applicable return and filing route with company counsel. Reconcile allottees, securities, consideration, resolutions and required valuation documents to bank and capitalization records. The authorized officer and certifying professional review and file the return through the current MCA process, then resolve any resubmission request. Match the final filing status to the transaction records.
options.when: Closing the priced round in India

options.title: UK - SH01 return of allotment
options.summary: Prepare the UK SH01 from the actual allotment date, share numbers and classes, amounts paid and resulting capital. The authorized officer or filing agent submits it through the current Companies House process and checks the acknowledgment. Reconcile the company’s ownership records to the allotment, and identify any accompanying constitutional or control filings required by the round.
options.when: Closing the priced round in the United Kingdom

options.title: Germany - notarized Kapitalerhoehung
options.summary: Work with the German notary and counsel on the resolutions, subscription declarations, contribution evidence and registry submission needed for this capital increase. Reconcile the documents with the articles, financing terms and allocations. The responsible signatories execute the package, and the filing owner tracks the register’s response. Record the increase in capitalization at the effective event counsel identifies.
options.when: Closing the priced round in Germany

options.title: France - augmentation de capital
options.summary: Determine the French capital-increase procedure from the company’s legal form and articles with counsel. Match allocations and contributions to the resolution, amended articles and required publication or filing documents. The authorized representative completes the applicable formalities and follows any correction request through acceptance. Reconcile the final capital and shareholder records with the completed transaction.
options.when: Closing the priced round in France

references.title: Service Public: augmenter le capital social

parts.title: Update the cap table and kick off the 409A refresh
parts.guidance: Update the equity system for the completed financing, converted instruments, issued shares and option-pool changes, reconciling it to the final closing schedule. The authorized equity owner resolves any difference from the legal documents. Give the valuation adviser the financing terms and other material changes to assess a refresh before later grants; the preferred financing price does not itself establish common-stock value.

metadata.supportReason: The term sheet, diligence, and approvals are human; the paperwork routing, signatures, share issuance, and cap-table updates run on APIs.

geoNotes.summary: A priced round is a private placement under Companies Act s.42: special resolution, a registered-valuer report on price, PAS-3 return of allotment to the MCA (fronted by NSWS — mca.gov.in blocks automated access), and FC-GPR reporting to the RBI within 30 days if the money is foreign.

Closing means allotting new shares: board and (usually) shareholder authorities, a subscription and shareholders' agreement, new articles for the preferred class, then the SH01 return of allotment filed at Companies House within a month.

A priced round is a notarized Kapitalerhöhung: the notary beurkundets the shareholder resolution and subscription, and the new shares only exist once the increase is registered in the Handelsregister — build notary lead time into the closing plan.

Closing is an augmentation de capital: an extraordinary general meeting, updated statuts, the funds certified on a blocked account, then the capital change filed through the guichet unique into the RCS.

A priced round is a shareholder-resolved aumento de capital registered at the commercial registry (online through Empresa Online) — notarization is generally no longer required for standard capital increases since the 2006 registry reform.

Closing means articles of amendment creating the preferred class plus a private placement under NI 45-106 exemptions — with the Form 45-106F1 report of exempt distribution due to the regulators within 10 days of closing.
